entities.summary:
Godehok (b. 450 CE) was a prominent economist and social scientist of the Classical era, active in the Global region. He was known for his work on the monarchs and rulers of the time, and his research contributed significantly to the understanding of the social structures of ancient civilizations.

Godehok's work was influential in shaping the field of economics, particularly in the area of comparative civilization. He was one of the first scholars to study the economic systems of ancient civilizations, and his research helped to establish the field of economic history.

Godehok's legacy can be seen in the many scholars who followed in his footsteps, including prominent economists and historians of the Classical era. His work continues to be studied and cited today, and his contributions to the field of economics remain significant.

One of the most striking statistics to emerge from Godehok's research is the average lifespan of a monarch during the Classical era, which was just 25 years. This finding had significant implications for our understanding of the social and political structures of ancient civilizations, and it continues to influence research in the field of economics today.
